payload.name: Preserve explicit emotional significance in extracted memories
payload.description: When a user explicitly states what an activity or object means to them (comfort, connection, coping), include that experiential claim in the extracted candidate and any memory update.
content: When a user explicitly states what an activity or object means to them—such as providing comfort, evoking a memory, or connecting them to someone—capture that experiential claim in the extracted candidate, not just the underlying factual belief.
When updating an existing memory with such a statement, merge the explicit emotional/relational significance into the updated content so it remains retrievable.

solves: The extraction candidate kept Deborah's mother's belief about art but dropped Deborah's explicit statement that art shows are comforting and make her feel she is still experiencing them with her mother. The reusable mechanism is that explicit self-reported emotional or relational significance is often omitted when candidates paraphrase a user's words into a general belief. This Skill applies to any construction session where a speaker explicitly states what an activity or object means to them, and guides extraction and enrichment to preserve that significance.
